column3: NASB renders “strike” as “strike down”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB has “His disciples”; the Greek has “the disciples.”
“Very sorrowful … until death” is rendered “deeply grieved, to the point of death.”
NASB adds “them” and a second “You will.”
NASB renders the commands as “keep watching and praying.”
NASB follows the critical text: “if this cannot pass away” without “cup” and “from Me.”
NASB adds “once more,” following the critical text’s “again.”
NASB renders the opening as a question (“Are you still sleeping and resting?”); the Greek can be read as a statement or command.
NASB follows the critical text and renders the terse “for what you are here” as “do what you have come for.”
NASB follows the critical text without “with you”; it renders the imperfect “I was sitting” as “I used to sit.”
NASB follows the critical text without “the elders”; “were seeking” is rendered “kept trying to obtain.”
NASB follows the critical text with “two,” without “false witnesses.”
